motivation: MS-119: Italy zero-label cache decoder macro IoU .089, below the registered [.15,.45]. Label audit (artifacts/label_size_audit.json): Italy landslide components median 11 px (10 m) vs 32-87 px in the 8 headline regions; 66% of Italy components are smaller than one 40 m token (16 px); 14.4 components per positive tile. Italy is therefore the regime where the token-resolution hypothesis (rejected on the 8 headline regions, MS-115) predicted a gain. This experiment isolates that.

arms.p4_upsample2: same 40 m cache, decoder grid doubled (control for grid size)
arms.p2_native: 20 m cache, REAL acquisition dates (olmo_italy_p2_rt; confirmatory tiles reused from olmo_base_p2_rt by symlink, Italy tiles newly extracted)
arms.p2_avgpool2: 20 m cache average-pooled back to 32x32 (removes fine grid)

decoder: cache_decoder_train.py, identical recipe, fold holdout_italy (loco_folds_italy.json), seeds 1-3
metrics: positive-tile macro IoU (primary, as MS-119), exact AP (secondary)

rule.resolution_helps_on_small_objects: p2_native > p4_native by >= .03 macro (seed mean) AND p2_native > p4_upsample2 by >= .02 AND p2_avgpool2 < p2_native by >= .02 -> the resolution lever is conditional on object size (small-object regime); write as a scoped claim, not a general one
rule.no: otherwise: Italy's low score is not a token-resolution problem; raw baseline / label-noise explanations remain
rule.next_regardless: raw UNet3D baseline and few-shot A1 (K=5,20) on Italy, adapter required (registered here, not yet runnable)

not_claimed: anything about the 8 headline regions (already rejected there)
gpu: extraction ~50 min (5,321 tiles patch 2), 9 decoder runs ~3 h, GPU1
